limitations: Ground anchors and road polygons are manual observations, not an implemented lane/geometry model.
The 50 is a different physical sign from the 30 repeated in the next two frames.
Equirectangular fixed-x positions are not comparable with a mounted phone camera; never score the legacy x threshold on these frames.
No legitimate mainline speed sign is visible in the selected approach; this subset cannot establish mainline recall.
Two-second still cadence is preserved; no frame duplication or invented vehicle speed/deceleration.
Geographic novelty is audited only against available repository manifests and drive corpora; overlap with upstream classifier training cannot be ruled out.
Current OSM references are a dated topology counterfactual and do not prove 2025 sign applicability.
Public host fallback: IGN items were discovered through the Panoramax federation because OSM France storage was unreachable.
Four non-ego observations cover two physical exit signs; these are not four independent sign encounters.
One real on-ramp observation is a legitimate-sign positive control; no cross-year physical identity is asserted.
Cadence is unusable for temporal tracking. Microsecond source timestamps are preserved without fabrication.
Current OSM topology and lane tags postdate capture; use as explicitly labeled counterfactual context only.
Legacy native map/fix diagnostics are unavailable for public images, so a native guard baseline is not observed.
Manual supplementary-arrow-to-road annotations are retained for review but excluded from the geometry-only experiment because they already contain a road relation.
Two geographic areas and four public capture sequences; repeated frames and opposing directions at one exit are not independent route samples.
